value.hook: Open before reviewing in-process parent/start reads that replace a ps snapshot, or trusting CI for a macOS kernel path.
value.title: Per-hop ancestry walks and macOS-only proof

sections.name: body
sections.value:
#300 (issue #85) replaced the identity routes' one `ps -Ao pid,ppid` snapshot with `proc::parent_of` reads, one hop at a time. My verdict was pass-with-notes.

- Grade a per-hop walk on its stops. Every stop must refuse: an unread parent, a parent of pid 1 or below, the hop limit (which also covers self-parents and cycles), and a spawn_blocking join error (`unwrap_or(false)`). A reparent can't produce a false match: it goes to 1 (refused) or to a Linux subreaper, which is already a real ancestor.
- Per-hop reads are not one snapshot: a chain pid can exit and be reused between two reads. It's not caller-steerable (macOS pids are sequential, so it needs a wrap within microseconds), and the old lsof-then-ps path had a wider window of the same class. So it's a note, not a block, but reject any comment that says the walk "can never invent" the host.
- CI is ubuntu only. The macOS `proc_pidinfo` paths are unproven until you run them yourself: `PIJ_SHARED_TARGET=$(bash harness/scripts/cargo-target.sh) just shared-build -- test -p pij-daemon --lib <filter>`. `identity_tests.rs` is a lib module: `--test '*'` silently finds 0 tests.
- `program::launch` resolves from the daemon's own PATH on first use and keeps only hits. Redirect risk equals the bare name's (the user's PATH dirs). The daemon never calls set_var("PATH").
- The bare-name sensor in `spawn_sites.rs` matches `Command::new("literal")` only. A const or variable gets past it.
